children: South Korean AI startup Upstage is considering a pre-IPO funding round as it prepares for a potential stock-market listing, according to a
“We are reviewing several capital market options, including an IPO, but there’s no fixed timeline or size yet,” co-founder and CTO Hwalsuk Lee said, “We are also considering a pre-IPO round.”

-backed Upstage has not set a timeline or size for a potential IPO or pre-IPO round. The Seoul-based startup raised 560B won ($420M) in a Series C financing this year, taking its total funding to 730B won.
Upstage has secured a partnership and strategic investment from Advanced Micro Devices
as it deepens its work with the chipmaker, although its capital requirements continue to grow as it competes in the hardware-intensive AI market.
Lee said Upstage’s latest Solar Pro 4 model is handling production traffic on AMD
graphics processing units, while joint optimization efforts with AMD have improved throughput by 25%, helping the model process more than 100 billion tokens of AI work per day.

The startup plans to increase the size of its AI models, expand support for Southeast Asian languages, and strengthen its agent capabilities. The company is also building a broader domestic AI stack through partnerships with South Korean AI chip designer FuriosaAI and deployments of its technology in large-scale consumer services.
“We are trying to prove ourselves in the global market,” Lee said. “Our latest model, Solar Pro 4, is seeing strong global adoption.”
